newsitem.title: USA: EIA revises down U.S. 1997 natgas demand outlook.
newsitem.headline: EIA revises down U.S. 1997 natgas demand outlook.

text.p: U.S. natural gas demand is expected to reach 22.18 trillion cubic feet in 1997, up 1.2 percent from 1996, the Energy Information Administration said Monday, lowering its previous demand forecast of 22.25 Tcf.
It also revised down its demand projection for 1998 to 23.08 Tcf, down from 23.23 Tcf, with growth seen at 4.1 percent compared with EIA's previous forecast of 4.4 percent.
Most of the increase in 1997 was expected to come in the industrial and utility sectors, EIA said in its quarterly short-term energy outlook.
Industrial demand in 1997 should grow by 3.5 percent to 8.9 Tcf "due to strong economic growth," it said.
EIA saw demand for natural gas in electric generation soaring 8.2 percent in 1997 to 3.16 Tcf, with several nuclear power plants shut down this summer.
Residential demand was forecast to fall by 5.0 percent in 1997 to 4.97 Tcf from high levels in 1996 largely because of this year's mild winter.

EIA expected strong natural gas prices next winter, and said that "additional demand pressure from either a particularly hot summer or early cold spell next fall could upset what is emerging as a rather delicate short-term balance for natural gas demand and supply."

The forecast pegged natural gas prices at the wellhead in 1997 at an average of $2.29 per thousand cubic feet, up from EIA's previous outlook of $2.24 and last year's average of $2.25, mainly due to a sharp price spike in the first quarter.
U.S. dry gas production in 1997 was projected to reach 19.14 Tcf, up slightly from 1996 but down from an earlier forecast of 19.19 Tcf.
The outlook assumed that U.S. Gross Domestic Product would grow by 3.7 percent in 1997 and by 1.8 percent in 1998.
